title: Functional equation
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$; let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and fix an
indeterminate $T$. For $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension.
Let $X_0/k_0$ be a
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected scheme of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$; put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $F$ be
geometric Frobenius. For every integer $i$
with $0\leq i\leq2d$, put

$$
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),
\qquad
F_{i,\ell}=F\vert_{V_{i,\ell}},
\qquad
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

Here $H^i(X,\Ql)$ is the
ordinary cohomology group.
These data form the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$. Put
$b_i=\deg P_i$ and define the
determinant constant
$D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)$. Define

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i,
\qquad
\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i},
\qquad
\varepsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}\Delta.
$$

Thus $\varepsilon$ is the
normalized functional-equation
sign. Define the point-count zeta
series by

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right).
$$

The alternating determinant scalar satisfies

$$
\Delta^2=q^{d\chi}.
$$

The normalized sign satisfies

$$
\varepsilon^2=1,\qquad \varepsilon\in\{1,-1\},
$$

and the zeta function satisfies

$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T).
$$

Equivalently, the determinant-constant form of the functional equation is

$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^\chi T^\chi
\left(\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\right)Z(X_0,T).
$$

proof.text:
*Step 1: the data and the integral factors.* The finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0=\Fq,k=\Fbar)$ is that of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and the hypotheses on $X_0$ (smooth of pure dimension $d$, proper, geometrically connected, with geometric fiber $X=X_0	imes_{k_0}k$) are those of [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]. For the fixed prime $\ell
eq p$, the spaces $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, the operators $F_{i,\ell}=F\vert_{V_{i,\ell}}$ and the polynomials $P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})\in\Ql[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, are the smooth-proper cohomological family of [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family], and $P_{i,\ell}$ is the reverse characteristic polynomial [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial] of $F_{i,\ell}$. By [prop-integral-recovery] (existence and uniqueness clause, applied to $X_0$) there are unique polynomials $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell')}=P_{i,\ell'}$ for every prime $\ell'
eq p$; they are the integral realization-independent factors of [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor], normalized by $P_i(0)=1$, and in particular $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for the fixed $\ell$. Conversely, a polynomial $P\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $P^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for the fixed $\ell$ alone equals $P_i$: $\mathbf Z	o\Ql$ is injective because $\Ql$ has characteristic zero [lem-weil-integers-injective-char-zero], so the coefficientwise extension $\mathbf Z[T]	o\Ql[T]$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension] is injective [lem-weil-coefficientwise-extension-injective], and $P^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}=P_i^{(\ell)}$ gives $P=P_i$. Hence 'the integral Frobenius factor with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$' of the statement is this $P_i$, whether the condition is read for the fixed $\ell$ or for every $\ell'
eq p$, and it is the polynomial that [prop-duality-reciprocity], [prop-weil-functional-equation-parity] and [def-weil-functional-equation-sign], applied below, take as their $P_i$ (each assumes the hypotheses of this statement on $X_0$ and takes $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ in the same way). The integers $b_i=\deg P_i$ are the Betti numbers of [def-weil-betti-numbers], and $D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)$, $\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i$ and $\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}$ are the determinant constants, the Euler characteristic and the alternating determinant scalar of [def-weil-determinant-constants], defined there by the same formulas. Since $P_i(0)=1$, [lem-weil-leading-coefficient-nonzero] gives $D_i\in\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}$, so $D_i^{-1}$ and $\Delta$ are elements of $\mathbf Q^	imes$; and $P_i
eq0$.

source.place: statement (the hypotheses and the definitions of $P_i$, $b_i$, $D_i$, $\chi$, $\Delta$); the identification of the statement's $P_i$ with the unique factors of prop-integral-recovery is left unsaid by the blueprint (slopmaster2 lists prop:integral-recovery among the uses of prop:functional-equation, 01_final_weil_conjectures.tex line 3525, without saying where it is used). Milne LEC, Summary 27.14 (d), p. 159: the $P_r\in1+t\mathbf Z[t]$ are independent of $\ell$.

proof.text:
*Step 2: the zeta series as a rational function.* By [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] with $Y_0=X_0$, $Z(X_0,T)=\exp\bigl(\sum_{n\geq1}\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})T^n/n\bigr)\in1+T\mathbf Q[[T]]$ is the point-count zeta series of the statement. The factorization clause of [prop-integral-recovery], for the $P_i$ of Step 1, gives

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T):
$$

that is, in the sense of [def-weil-rational-power-series], $Z(X_0,T)$ is a rational power series (each $P_i$ has $P_i(0)=1$, so the even-indexed product is a denominator with nonzero constant term) whose rational function $R_Z\in\mathbf Q(T)$ is the displayed product; every assertion 'in $\mathbf Q(T)$' about $Z(X_0,T)$ is the assertion about $R_Z$. The expression $Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})$ in the statement is the image of $R_Z$ under the substitution of $q^{-d}T^{-1}$ for $T$ [def-weil-rational-function-field] (with $c=q^{-d}\in\mathbf Q^\times$), which is an involutive $\mathbf Q$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $\mathbf Q(T)$; likewise $P(q^{-d}T^{-1})$ for a polynomial $P$ is its evaluation at $q^{-d}T^{-1}$, that is, $\sigma(P)$. (The imported proof derived the product from [prop-trace-determinant], which gives it only with the $\ell$-adic factors $P_{i,\ell}$ after the coefficient extension $\mathbf Q[[T]]\to\Ql[[T]]$; the identity with the integral $P_i$ in $\mathbf Q(T)$ is the factorization clause of prop-integral-recovery, whose proof uses prop-trace-determinant through thm-weil-realization-independence.)

source.place: ## Proof, step 1 ('identifies it with the normalized product $Z(X_0,T)=\prod_iP_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$. All subsequent manipulations therefore take place in ... $\mathbf Q(T)$'); the descent from $\Ql$ to $\mathbf Q(T)$ is prop-integral-recovery. Milne LEC, Summary 27.14 (a), (b), (d), p. 159: $Z(X_0,t)\in\mathbf Q(t)$, $Z=P_1P_3\cdots P_{2d-1}/P_0P_2\cdots P_{2d}$ with $P_r\in1+t\mathbf Z[t]$ independent of $\ell$.

proof.text:
*Step 3: the degreewise reciprocity, as hypotheses of the algebraic lemma.* [prop-duality-reciprocity], applied to $X_0$, the fixed prime $\ell$ and the $P_i$ of Step 1, states that for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$

$$
b_i=b_{2d-i},\qquad D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i},\qquad
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}].
$$

The Laurent polynomial ring $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$ is the subring of $\mathbf Q(T)$ generated by $\mathbf Q[T]$ and $T^{-1}$ (the inverse of $T$ in the field $\mathbf Q(T)$), and $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})$ is the evaluation of $P_{2d-i}$ at $q^{-d}T^{-1}\in\mathbf Q(T)$, that is, $\sigma(P_{2d-i})$ for the substitution $\sigma$ of Step 2 [def-weil-rational-function-field]; so the last identity is an identity in $\mathbf Q(T)$. Put $K=\mathbf Q$ and $c=q^d\in\mathbf Q^\times$, so that $c^{-1}T^{-1}=q^{-d}T^{-1}$ and $c^{b_i}=q^{db_i}$. The three displayed relations are then exactly hypotheses 1, 2 and 3 of [lem-weil-alternating-product-reciprocity] for the data $(P_i,b_i,D_i)_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ of Step 1, which satisfy $P_i\in\mathbf Q[T]$, $P_i(0)=1$, $b_i\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $D_i\in\mathbf Q^\times$ (Step 1); and the $\chi$, $\Delta$ and $Z(T)=\prod_iP_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ of that lemma are the $\chi$ and $\Delta$ of Step 1 and the $R_Z$ of Step 2.

source.place: ## Proof, step 2, first sentence ('The reciprocity relations in [prop-duality-reciprocity] give $b_i=b_{2d-i}$, $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$, ...'). Milne LEC, proof of Theorem 27.12, p. 158 (if $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s$ are the eigenvalues of $F$ on $H^r$ then $q^d/\alpha_1,\ldots,q^d/\alpha_s$ are those on $H^{2d-r}$); Deligne Weil I, (2.4), p. 281.

proof.text:
*Step 4: the determinant-constant form, and $\Delta^2=q^{d\chi}$.* By Step 3, [lem-weil-alternating-product-reciprocity] applies with $K=\mathbf Q$ and $c=q^d$. Its assertion (b) reads

$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})=\sigma(R_Z)=(-1)^\chi\,T^\chi\,\Delta\,Z(X_0,T)
=(-1)^\chi T^\chi\left(\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\right)Z(X_0,T)\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T),
$$

which is the determinant-constant form of the functional equation asserted in the statement. Its assertion (a) reads $\Delta^2=c^\chi=(q^d)^\chi=q^{d\chi}$ in $\mathbf Q^\times$, the first assertion of the statement.

source.place: ## Proof, step 2, first display (the reindexed product giving $Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})=(-1)^\chi T^\chi(\prod_iD_i^{(-1)^i})Z(X_0,T)$) and last display ($\Delta^2=\prod_i(D_iD_{2d-i})^{(-1)^i}=q^{d\chi}$); the computation itself is the new lemma. Milne LEC, Theorem 27.12, p. 158 ('This implies the statement'); Deligne Weil I, (2.6), p. 281 ('On déduit facilement ...').

proof.text:
*Step 5: parity of $d\chi$ and the normalized sign.* [prop-weil-functional-equation-parity], applied to $X_0$ and the $P_i$ of Step 1 (its $b_i$ and $\chi$ are those of Step 1), states that $d\chi$ is even: $d\chi=2h$ for an integer $h$. Hence $q^{-d\chi/2}=q^{-h}$ and $q^{d\chi/2}=q^{h}$ are elements of $\mathbf Q^\times$, and the data $(q,d,(P_i)_{0\leq i\leq2d})$ satisfy the hypotheses of [def-weil-functional-equation-sign] ($P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $P_i(0)=1$, $d\chi$ even). That definition computes $b_i$, $D_i$, $\chi$ and $\Delta$ by the formulas of Step 1 and defines

$$
\varepsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{-h}\Delta=(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}\Delta\in\mathbf Q^\times,
$$

which is the $\varepsilon$ of the statement: the normalized functional-equation sign.

source.place: ## Proof, step 2, from 'These same reciprocity relations show that $d\chi$ is even' to '$\varepsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}\Delta$'; the inline parity argument is replaced by prop-weil-functional-equation-parity (slopmaster2: prop:functional-equation-parity, 01_final_weil_conjectures.tex lines 3486-3494, listed among the uses of prop:functional-equation at line 3526). Deligne Weil I, (2.6), p. 281: 'l'entier $n\chi(X)$ est donc toujours pair'.

proof.text:
*Step 6: $\varepsilon^2=1$ and $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$.* Squaring the formula of Step 5 in $\mathbf Q^\times$ and using $2h=d\chi$ and Step 4(a),

$$
\varepsilon^2=(-1)^{2\chi}\,q^{-2h}\,\Delta^2=1\cdot q^{-d\chi}\cdot q^{d\chi}=1 .
$$

Since $\mathbf Q$ is a field, $0=\varepsilon^2-1=(\varepsilon-1)(\varepsilon+1)$ forces $\varepsilon=1$ or $\varepsilon=-1$; so $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$.

source.place: ## Proof, step 3. Milne LEC, Theorem 27.12, p. 158 (the sign $\pm$); Deligne Weil I, (2.6), p. 281 ($\varepsilon=\pm1$).

proof.text:
*Step 7: the sign form.* Multiplying the formula $\varepsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{-h}\Delta$ of Step 5 by $q^{h}$ gives $(-1)^\chi\Delta=\varepsilon\,q^{h}=\varepsilon\,q^{d\chi/2}$ in $\mathbf Q^\times$. Substituting this into the identity of Step 4,

$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})=\varepsilon\,q^{d\chi/2}\,T^\chi\,Z(X_0,T)\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T),
$$

which is the functional equation in its sign form. Together with Steps 4 and 6 this proves every assertion of the statement: $\Delta^2=q^{d\chi}$, $\varepsilon^2=1$, $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$, the sign form, and the equivalent determinant-constant form (the two forms differ by the substitution $(-1)^\chi\Delta=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}$ just made, which is invertible, so each implies the other).

source.place: ## Proof, step 4. Milne LEC, Theorem 27.12, p. 158: $Z(X_0,1/q^dt)=\pm q^{d\chi/2}t^\chi Z(X_0,t)$; Deligne Weil I, (2.6), p. 281, the same identity solved for $Z(X_0,t)$.

proof_origin.place: ## Proof (the blueprint's four steps, rewritten in seven: the imported step 1 cited prop-trace-determinant for an identity that only prop-integral-recovery gives; the imported step 2 is now Steps 3-5, with the substitution computation isolated as lem-weil-alternating-product-reciprocity and the inline parity argument replaced by prop-weil-functional-equation-parity; the imported steps 3 and 4 are Steps 6 and 7). The slopmaster2 blueprint states the proposition without a proof (01_final_weil_conjectures.tex lines 3523-3551). Human sources of the result, which state it and leave the substitution computation to the reader: literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf, Theorem 27.12 and Remark 27.13, pp. 158-159; literature/deligne-weil-I_PMIHES-1974-43.pdf, (2.4)-(2.6), p. 281.

split_report.summary: Statement kept verbatim: it is the master text, and the slopmaster2 LaTeX (prop:functional-equation, 01_final_weil_conjectures.tex lines 3523-3551, stated for a smooth-proper datum without a proof) asserts the same three things except that it omits the clause Delta^2 = q^{d chi}, which the master statement has and the proof gives; checked against Milne LEC Theorem 27.12 / Remark 27.13 (pp. 158-159) and Deligne Weil I (2.4)-(2.6) (p. 281), and on X_0 = P^1 (b = (1,0,1), D = (1,1,q), chi = 2, Delta = q, Delta^2 = q^2 = q^{d chi}, epsilon = 1, Z(1/(qT)) = qT^2 Z(T)) and on d = 0 (X_0 a point: P_0 = 1 - T, b_0 = 1, D_0 = 1, chi = 1, Delta = 1, epsilon = -1, Z = 1/(1-T), Z(T^{-1}) = -T Z(T)). No Lean on either branch. Proof rewritten in seven steps. What was wrong in the imported proof: step 1 cited prop-trace-determinant for Z(X_0,T) = prod P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}} in Q(T), but that proposition gives the product only with the ell-adic factors P_{i,ell} after coefficient extension to Q_ell[[T]]; the identity with the integral P_i in Q(T) is the factorization clause of prop-integral-recovery (slopmaster2 lists prop:integral-recovery among the uses), now Step 2, and prop-trace-determinant is dropped from the proof. Step 2 of the import proved the parity of d chi inline; that is now the reviewed node prop-weil-functional-equation-parity (Step 5), as the brief says. The substitution computation (reindex i -> 2d-i under T -> q^{-d}T^{-1}, collect (-1)^chi T^chi Delta, and Delta^2 = prod (D_i D_{2d-i})^{(-1)^i} = q^{d chi}) was sketched in two displays with the sign bookkeeping ((-1)^{b_i (-1)^{i+1}} = (-1)^{b_i}, prod (-1)^{b_i} = (-1)^chi) left unsaid; it is pure field algebra, which both Milne ('This implies the statement') and Deligne ('On déduit facilement') leave to the reader, so it is now the new statement node lem-weil-alternating-product-reciprocity over a field K with c in K^x (Steps 3-4 are its hypotheses and its conclusion). Also made explicit: that the statement's P_i (defined by P_i^{(ell)} = P_{i,ell} for the one fixed ell) is the unique factor of prop-integral-recovery (injectivity of Z[T] -> Q_ell[T]), so that prop-duality-reciprocity, the parity proposition and the sign definition apply to it (Step 1); that Z(X_0,T) is read in Q(T) through def-weil-rational-power-series and Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1}) is the substitution automorphism of def-weil-rational-function-field (Step 2); and that the Laurent identity of prop-duality-reciprocity is read in Q(T) (Step 3). stmt_deps rebuilt from the notions the statement names: kept the seven imported ids and added def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius (F on H^i, as def-weil-determinant-constants does), def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial, def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-coefficientwise-extension, def-weil-betti-numbers, def-weil-polynomial-coefficient, def-weil-determinant-constants, lem-weil-leading-coefficient-nonzero (D_i^{-1} and Delta need D_i != 0), prop-weil-functional-equation-parity (epsilon needs d chi even), def-weil-functional-equation-sign, def-weil-point-counts-zeta, def-weil-rational-power-series and def-weil-rational-function-field (the sense of 'in Q(T)' and of Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})).
